answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an AI economy can enforce proof-of-inference challenges. Rather than letting rogue nodes drift through like a fleeting zephyr, validators require agents to solve verifiable cognitive tasks, such as parsing an assigned sonnet. An attacker must expend scarce GPU cycles and electricity per identity, while failing nodes receive an umber warning flag. However, this mechanism disadvantages lightweight edge agents and cannot deter well-funded adversaries.
